theme: US sunbelt and mountain STR markets datasets: Florida (Orlando, Miami, Tampa), Arizona (Scottsdale, Sedona), Texas, Colorado (Breckenridge, Denver), Tennessee (Gatlinburg), Great Smoky Mountains

candidates.name: Florida-Airbnb (CrystalVF)
candidates.what_it_holds: Capstone project analyzing Broward County (Fort Lauderdale, used as a South Florida / Miami-area proxy) Inside Airbnb data, snapshot dated 2025-06-24. data/raw/ has listings.csv.gz and calendar.csv.gz committed directly to the repo (plus a DATA_SOURCE_LINKS.md); data/clean/ is empty placeholders. README frames it around ADR, occupancy rate, RevPAL as KPIs. R/SQL/scripts folders for the analysis pipeline.
candidates.why_useful: A committed, single-date Inside Airbnb snapshot for a Florida sunbelt market (Broward/South Florida) we do not explicitly hold in our 13-city or 120-market cohorts; could extend geographic coverage for gap-relevant Florida ADR/occupancy checks, though it is only one snapshot date and duplicates our existing Inside Airbnb methodology rather than adding a new data type.
candidates.duplicate_of_holding: Same Inside Airbnb source/methodology we already hold for other cities, but this specific Florida market and date are not in our current panel

candidates.name: Generating-Florida-AirBNBs-Insights
candidates.what_it_holds: A single Tableau packaged workbook ('AirBNB in Florida Insights.twbx', repo ~14MB) plus a README, pushed April 2022. Tableau .twbx files bundle an internal data extract (often Inside Airbnb-derived) but the raw rows are not directly exposed as CSV without opening in Tableau or unzipping the .twbx.
candidates.why_useful: Potentially an older (2022, pre-2023) Florida Airbnb listings snapshot, which would be valuable under gap #1 (historical/archived Inside Airbnb dumps), but the data is locked inside a proprietary Tableau extract format with no README detail on source date, city, or fields, making it low-confidence and low-accessibility.

candidates.name: airdna-scraper (BigAnomaly / Apify actor)
candidates.what_it_holds: An Apify actor (README only, no code visible in the default branch listing beyond README) that enriches a list of Airbnb listing URLs with AirDNA revenue, occupancy, ADR, and revenue-potential figures. Requires an existing AirDNA account and a bearer token copied from the browser session (app.airdna.co), plus an AirDNA market ID for revenue/occupancy fields. Outputs one record per listing with listing_id, market, listing_type, bedrooms/bathrooms/accommodates, rating, and the AirDNA metrics.
candidates.why_useful: Directly targets gap #2 (realised ADR/occupancy for STRs from AirDNA-type sources) at the listing level, which is exactly the metric class we are missing; however it requires an authenticated AirDNA account (paid product) and manually harvested bearer token, so it is a method pointer, not a free dataset, and running it would be a terms-of-service question for a human.
candidates.geography: Any AirDNA-covered market, so applicable to all Sunbelt/mountain markets in this theme

candidates.name: airdna-scraper (nishantshah2112)
candidates.what_it_holds: A short (7KB) Playwright/Python script (airdna_scraper.py) that logs into app.airdna.co with an email/password pair read from a .env file (AIRDNA_EMAIL/AIRDNA_PASSWORD) and navigates to a market overview page; the actual scraping/extraction logic is stubbed out ('keeping it short for upload guide ... scraping logic goes here'), so it is an incomplete login-automation skeleton rather than a working data puller.
candidates.why_useful: Same target as the Apify actor above (AirDNA revenue/occupancy/ADR, gap #2) but incomplete, and it requires typing a real AirDNA username/password into an automation script, which is a credential-handling and ToS concern; flagged for completeness only, not something to run.
candidates.geography: Any AirDNA-covered market (example URL points at a generic 'airdna-405' market id)

notes: This run hit unusually bad tooling conditions: WebSearch reported its shared session budget (200/200) was already exhausted on the very first query, before any theme-specific search executed, so none of the four suggested WebSearch queries (or their broader variants) actually ran. The fallback DuckDuckGo HTML endpoint (html.duckduckgo.com) was unreachable (ECONNREFUSED) from this environment. Bing search via WebFetch worked mechanically but appears to silently drop the 'site:github.com' operator (results were generic tourism/travel pages, not filtered to GitHub), making it useless for repo discovery. Direct GitHub search pages (github.com/search?q=...) via WebFetch returned HTTP 429 (rate-limited, Retry-After 3600s). That left `gh search repos` as the only working discovery path; it was rate-limited once (HTTP 403, user-level API rate limit) after ~9 calls, recovered after a 40s sleep per the fallback protocol, but continued to return empty result sets for the large majority of Sunbelt/mountain-specific queries (Scottsdale, Sedona, Gatlinburg, Breckenridge, Denver, Orlando, Texas, Arizona, Smoky Mountains, county-level STR registries) — i.e. genuine absence of matching public repos on those exact terms, not just a tooling failure, though a differently-phrased or paginated `gh search` might still surface something. Net yield for this theme is thin (4 real candidates, only one a genuine committed dataset). Two clear negative findings worth recording for other scouts: (1) DWConnolly/tampa-airbnb, despite its name, is a vacation-rental marketing website (React/Vite) with no Airbnb data — exclude if it resurfaces; (2) both AirDNA scraper repos require a personal paid AirDNA login (bearer token or email/password), so neither is a free-data source — they are method pointers only, consistent with gap #2's framing ('AirDNA ... sample exports') and should not be run per the catalogue-only rule. Suggest a re-run of this theme once the shared WebSearch budget resets, since none of the assigned keyword-hint queries were ever actually executed via WebSearch.
